_about: Every number on the W2 slides traces back to a key in this file. Generated by slides/scripts/make_figs_w02.py; do not edit by hand.

aliasing.rule: alias = fs - f for fs/2 < f < fs

consistency.note: two-dimensional cartoon of alternating projections; the real sets live in C^(F×T)

demo2.caveat: one 5-second utterance, one speaker, one microphone. Orders of magnitude, not benchmarks.
demo2.stft: 25 ms Hann, 10 ms hop, N = 512, 16 kHz; least-squares ISTFT; Griffin-Lim without momentum, seed 0

frame_rate_ladder.note: 4× subsampling and 12.5 Hz are typical examples (W4, W6), not properties of every system

hann_lobes.note: D(f) drawn in its large-L limit sin(πu)/(πu), u = fL/fs; the zero positions k·fs/L are exact for any L. Hann = ½D(f) − ¼D(f − fs/L) − ¼D(f + fs/L), so its first zero moves from fs/L to 2fs/L.

masking.note: shape only. The quiet-threshold curve uses Terhardt's approximation as commonly quoted; the spreading slopes are illustrative, not a psychoacoustic model

source_filter.note: net tilt −6 dB/oct = glottal −12 dB/oct plus lip radiation +6 dB/oct; a textbook idealisation

stop_structure.note: durations are illustrative; the slide gives orders of magnitude only

three_representations.note: 768 × 50 Hz is the HuBERT/wav2vec 2.0 base configuration; 8 × 12.5 Hz is the Mimi codec as used in the W6 outline. Both are examples, to be verified when W5 and W6 are built.

tones.note: Chao tone numerals for Mandarin citation tones are standard. The right panel is a cartoon of declination and a final rise superimposed on lexical tones — shapes are illustrative, not measured.

vowel_space.source: Peterson & Barney, JASA 24:175–184, 1952 — averages for adult male speakers
vowel_space.verification: values confirmed from a secondary source only (Princeton CS325 course page), 2026-09-17
